objective: DIAGNOSE warehouse transform+material mismatch (read-only, NO mutation/build/sync). METHOD: write and run a Python script to do the deterministic comparison - do NOT reason through all parts in one pass. GROUND TRUTH=canonical RBXMX src/ServerStorage/GeneratedAssets/abandoned_warehouse_interior_01.rbxmx (original correct warehouse, nested 107 wrapper Models, plain XML not zip). BROKEN=generated src/Workspace/abandoned_warehouse_interior_01.model.json (62 MeshParts, 2 SurfaceAppearance, all Material=Concrete/Anchored), made by flattening the 107 Models. Studio symptom: EXPLODED/DEFORMED/MISASSEMBLED + LARGELY WHITE. Do NOT assume flattening was lossless. In the script: parse RBXMX XML, for each of the 62 MeshParts compute its WORLD CFrame (product of all ancestor CFrames from root to part) and compare to the model.json CFrame; also compare Name, MeshId, Size, PivotOffset/WorldPivot/ModelMeshCFrame, scale props, SurfaceAppearance parent+texture props, Color/Material/TextureID. Print a per-part diff table + a summary of the dominant mismatch pattern. Find EXACT root cause of (1) exploded/deformed (transform) and (2) largely white (material/texture). Report root cause per symptom + exact fix (which parts, what CFrame/Size/Material/TextureID/SurfaceAppearance values) + whether fix is a global rule (re-bake all CFrames from canonical) or per-part. No file changes.
acceptance_criteria: Compact handoff: (1) root cause of exploded/deformed with the specific transform property mismatch (ancestor CFrame not baked / wrong pivot / scale), (2) root cause of largely white with the specific material/texture mismatch (Material=Concrete overriding SurfaceAppearance / wrong TextureID / SA not parented), (3) exact deterministic fix: which parts + what values, and whether it is a global re-bake rule or a per-part list, (4) evidence: 3-5 sample MeshParts showing canonical world CFrame vs model.json CFrame + canonical material/texture vs model.json material/texture. No file changes made.
